title: Making distant LOD (object LOD) for a static object in Fallout 4
content:
Making distant LOD (object LOD) for a static object in Fallout 4
Distant LOD meshes are separate NIF files, one per level, named <Name>_LOD_0.nif, <Name>_LOD_1.nif, <Name>_LOD_2.nif and kept under Meshes\LOD\ (for example Meshes\LOD\Architecture\Shacks\). Vanilla keeps their textures under Textures\LOD\ and their materials under Materials\LOD\, small and separate from the full-detail textures.
Keep them very low: across 900 vanilla LOD meshes the median _LOD_0 is 8 triangles, 90% are 125 or fewer, the largest is about 2,200 (the USS Constitution), and city buildings use roughly 150-450.
A LOD material must not point at the full-size textures: if the LOD NIF still names the object's own .bgsm, the game draws the 4K textures on every LOD, because the .bgsm overrides the textures in the NIF.
Attaching them (do NOT make a separate STAT for a LOD mesh):
1. Open the object's own STAT record, the one with the full-detail model that you place in the world.
2. Tick Has Distant LOD, click Specify distant LOD meshes..., and set level 0, 1 and 2 to the _LOD_0/1/2 meshes.
3. Generate object LOD for the worldspace (in the Creation Kit or with xLODGen). The game only shows LOD from that generated data.
If you copy a vanilla LOD STAT (for example CambridgeBuilding05_LOD) and point it at your LOD mesh, the preview stays empty: those records have Is Marker ticked, and markers are not drawn.
Flat billboard LODs (_LOD_FLAT) are for trees: only two vanilla meshes use one, both maple trees. Buildings and props use real LOD meshes.
tags: lod object lod distant lod has distant lod specify distant lod meshes xlodgen stat lod_0 lod_1 lod_2 billboard is marker meshes\lod
verified_by: Scan of all 900 NIFs under Meshes\LOD in the unpacked vanilla Data folder (triangle counts, texture and material paths, shader flags 0x80000201/0x1, _LOD_FLAT count). Creation Kit test 2026-11-03: a STAT copied from CambridgeBuilding05_LOD showed an empty preview; setting the LOD meshes on the house STAT worked.

title: Why LODs made by decimating fall apart on plants and buildings made of many pieces
content:
Why LODs made by decimating fall apart on plants and buildings made of many pieces
Decimate removes triangles piece by piece. A model made of hundreds of thin separate pieces (tendrils, leaves, spikes, a building overgrown with plant meshes) breaks into floating shards at LOD triangle counts, and its silhouette disappears.
A better LOD for such models is one solid simplified skin: voxel-remesh the whole model, drop tiny loose bits, decimate that skin to the target count, UV-unwrap it and bake the original's colour and normal maps onto it. Measured on a 7,700-triangle overgrown house (outline overlap with the original from 12 views): solid skin 0.83 / 0.83 / 0.87 at 1,500 / 500 / 150 triangles, decimation 0.81 / 0.61 / 0.08.
The Mossy Blender add-on 5.4.5 does this by default (LOD generator, method Solid Shell): it writes _LOD_0/1/2 NIFs with their own baked textures (1K / 512 / 256) and .bgsm files under Meshes\LOD, Textures\LOD and Materials\LOD. Set its output folder to the mod's root folder (the one that holds Meshes and Textures); a folder inside the mod is cut back to the root automatically. Versions before 5.4.5 decimated, kept the full-size material and saved PNG textures the game cannot load.

title: Textures come out darker after converting PNG/TGA to DDS with texconv (use -srgb)
content:
Textures come out darker after converting PNG/TGA to DDS with texconv (use -srgb)
texconv treats a PNG or TGA as sRGB and, when writing a normal (UNORM) DDS format, converts it to linear. The result is visibly darker, and normal maps get distorted. Measured: a diffuse averaging 0.168 came out at 0.050; a normal map pixel (0.25, 0.5) came out at (0.05, 0.22).
Fix: add -srgb to the texconv command (texconv -y -f BC7_UNORM -srgb -o <folder> <file>). It keeps the values as they are, and the output format stays the same (DXT1, DXT5, BC5 and BC7_UNORM were checked). Converting DDS back to PNG is not affected.
The Mossy Blender add-on before 5.4.5 converted without -srgb, so textures it converted from PNG/TGA may be too dark and their normal maps off; convert or export them again with 5.4.5.

verified_by: Measured 2026-11-02 with the texconv shipped with FO4Edit 4.1.5q: mean pixel values of PNG -> DDS -> PNG round trips with and without -srgb, DDS header formats checked.

title: Leaf cards and see-through plant parts: alpha cutout and two-sided in the NIF, the .bgsm and Blender
content:
Leaf cards and see-through plant parts: alpha cutout and two-sided in the NIF, the .bgsm and Blender
A leaf card is a flat mesh whose diffuse texture's alpha channel cuts out the leaf shape. It needs the cutout and two-sided set in both places the game reads:
- In the NIF: a NiAlphaProperty with alpha test on (vanilla uses flags 4844 with a threshold around 127-128), and the shader's DOUBLE_SIDED flag.
- In the .bgsm: alpha test on with its threshold, and two-sided on. The .bgsm overrides the NIF, so if it has alpha test off the cutout does not show.
In Blender with PyNifly, a mesh loaded from a NIF uses PyNifly's own 'Fallout 4 MTS' shader group: textures are image nodes named Diffuse_Texture, Normal_Texture, Specular_Texture and Glow_Map_Texture feeding its Diffuse, Normal, Smooth Spec and Glow Map inputs. The cutout is the 'Alpha Property' node (Alpha Test on/off, Alpha Threshold 0-255), and PyNifly writes the NiAlphaProperty from it on export. The .bgsm path is the material property BSLSP_Shader_Name, and the shader flags are the Shader_Flags_1 / Shader_Flags_2 properties. Don't plug a Principled BSDF into such a material's output: that disconnects the NIF shader and its textures.
The Mossy Blender add-on 5.4.5's 'Set Up as Leaf Card' keeps the mesh's textures and material and adds all of this, including switching on alpha test and two-sided in the existing .bgsm (the original is kept as .bgsm.bak; game files are never edited).

verified_by: Vanilla ShackBalconyFloor01_LOD_0.nif NiAlphaProperty flags 4844 threshold 127 and ShackLOD01.BGSM alpha test on (read with PyNifly / the add-on's BGSM reader); PyNifly 27 shaders.blend group inputs and shader_io.py import/export code; leaf-card export of copies of MossShrub02 and Creosote01 compared with a plain export 2026-11-03.

title: Creation Kit crashes from Blender-exported collision (empty compressed mesh, 'Instance should have already been created')
content:
Creation Kit crashes from Blender-exported collision (empty compressed mesh, 'Instance should have already been created')
Two collision exports crash the Creation Kit:
1. Exact-mesh / building collision written by PyNifly (v27 and v28) as hknpCompressedMeshShape: PyNifly leaves the shape's search tree empty at every size, while all 167,285 vanilla compressed meshes have it filled. The CK crashes inside the Havok loader. Exporting that collision as a convex hull (up to 128 vertices) instead loads fine.
2. A building whose collision pieces are all bodies of one bhkPhysicsSystem, as PyNifly writes it: placing it crashes with 'Instance should have already been created' (bhknpcollisionobject.cpp line 611), because Havok rejects the physics data and the system ends up with no instance. Giving each piece its own single-body bhkPhysicsSystem loads fine; vanilla precombined meshes carry up to 590 such systems.
The Mossy Blender add-on 5.4.4 fixed the first and 5.4.5 the second. Plain vanilla facts for reference: collision objects use flags 128, and BSXFlags 0x82 is the usual value for plants with collision.
If the crash continues after re-exporting, check that the Creation Kit is not still reading an older copy of the NIF from another mod in Mod Organizer.
tags: collision crash creation kit havok compressed mesh bhkphysicssystem bhknpcollisionobject instance should have already been created building pieces convex hull pynifly
verified_by: Vanilla scan of 167,285 compressed meshes and the multi-piece collision layout; CKPE crash dumps and CK disassembly of bhkNPCollisionObject::CreateInstance; Creation Kit tests 2026-11-02: a plant with collision and a 320-piece building (one system per piece) both load.

title: Walking through plants that were given collision in Blender (plants merged into a cliff or rock that already has collision)
content:
Walking through plants that were given collision in Blender (plants merged into a cliff or rock that already has collision)
Symptom: plants added to a bigger model (for example fungus plants merged into a cliff NIF) were given collision in the Mossy Blender add-on, but in game the player walks straight through them, while the same plants exported on their own do block the player.
Cause 1 (fixed in add-on 5.5.2): the model's root node already had Havok collision (the cliff's own compressed mesh). After export the add-on attaches convex-hull collision itself, and before 5.5.2 it skipped that step whenever the root already had collision, so only the cliff's collision reached the file. Check it in NifSkope: a plant with working collision has its own NiNode with a bhkNPCollisionObject and its own bhkPhysicsSystem. If the plants have none, the file has no collision for them.
Cause 2 (also fixed in 5.5.2): when several plants are one mesh object, a single convex hull around all of them fills the empty space between the plants with an invisible wall. The add-on now gives a mesh made of separate pieces one hull per plant: a small piece (a cap, a leaf) joins a bigger piece only when at least half of its bounding box is inside that piece, and there are at most 32 pieces per mesh.
How the fixed file is laid out (the same layout vanilla uses for several collision objects in one NIF): the existing collision stays where it is, and every new piece gets its own NiNode under the root with a bhkNPCollisionObject (flags 128, body 0) and its own single-body bhkPhysicsSystem. One physics system per piece is required; several bodies in one system crash the Creation Kit.
Fix: update the add-on to 5.5.2, select the plant mesh, run Add Collision again, then export the whole model again (all pieces as one NIF). Make sure the new NIF is the one the game loads (no older copy winning in Mod Organizer's left pane), and keep BSXFlags with the Havok bit (2) set: the cliff's own collision already sets it.
Plants with collision that sit in their own NIF already worked before 5.5.2, because there the root had no collision of its own.
tags: collision walk through plants no collision in game cliff rock merged plants convex hull invisible wall bhkphysicssystem bhknpcollisionobject add collision export blender add-on 5.5.2
verified_by: 2026-11-11: real cliff NIF with plants merged in: before the fix the plant meshes had no collision node; after re-export with the fixed add-on the file has 21 bhkNPCollisionObject / 21 bhkPhysicsSystem (6 original compressed meshes kept, 15 convex hulls each inside its plant's bounds), BSXFlags unchanged. Merged plant mesh: 54 loose parts -> 15 hulls, 6 of them one per large plant.

title: Collision made in Blender sits beside the model instead of on it (tree or plant inside an imported NIF)
content:
Collision made in Blender sits beside the model instead of on it (tree or plant inside an imported NIF)
Symptom: after Add Collision or Custom Collision on one piece of an imported model (for example a fungus tree that is part of a cliff NIF), the UCX_ collision object appears off to the side, lower or turned compared to the mesh, and in game the collision is somewhere other than the tree.
Cause: imported NIFs keep their node tree in Blender, so a mesh can sit under parent nodes that are moved and rotated (here a node turned 63 degrees). The Mossy Blender add-on's collision tools parented the new collision so that it kept only the mesh's own local offset and lost every transform above it; the collision ended up about 600 units to the side and 560 units down. Meshes directly under the root were not affected, because there that chain does nothing.
Fix: add-on 5.5.2 keeps the collision exactly on the mesh whatever its parent nodes do (all collision tools: Add Collision, Custom Collision, collision from LOD, compound and multi-piece). Delete the misplaced UCX_ object and generate the collision again. Check: the UCX_ wireframe must wrap the mesh in the viewport; after export the hull's position in the NIF must match the shape's.
Tip for trees and mushroom clusters: Add Collision gives each separate plant its own convex hull; Custom (exact mesh) collision is exported as one convex hull around everything, which covers the gaps between separate mushrooms.
tags: collision wrong place offset beside tree moved rotated parent node ucx blender add collision custom collision cliff tree mushroom
verified_by: 2026-11-11: a modder's Blender scene: tree at x -15.14..-9.73 (Blender units), old collision -6.02..1.25; after the fix Add Collision -15.11..-9.75, Custom -14.49..-10.08, compound slices inside the tree; exported NIF tree -1059..-681, hull -1057..-682 (game units).

title: Cliff or rock texture suddenly looks like one big stretched texture, grass looks wrong after re-exporting from Blender (UVs were repacked into 0-1)
content:
Cliff or rock texture suddenly looks like one big stretched texture, grass looks wrong after re-exporting from Blender (UVs were repacked into 0-1)
Symptom: after a re-export from Blender, a cliff, rock or ground piece shows its texture once, stretched over the whole model instead of repeating, and grass or plant cards show the wrong parts of their texture. Nothing changed in the BGSM or the DDS files.
Cause: the mesh's UV map was rebuilt. Landscape pieces tile their texture with UVs far outside 0-1 (a vanilla-style cliff piece ran from about -4 to +5), and grass cards also reach past the square (-0.17 to 1.22). Any UV tool that unwraps or packs islands (Smart UV Project, Pack Islands, Re-Unwrap, Lightmap Pack) squeezes every island into one 0-1 square, so the texture stops tiling and the cards point at the wrong spots. A rebuilt unwrap also adds UV seams, so the exported shape has more vertices than before (220 -> 268 on one cliff piece, 562 -> 605 on a grass card) while the triangles stay the same.
How to check: in NifSkope or Blender's UV editor compare the shape's UVs with the original NIF. Tiling UVs well outside 0-1 that are now all inside 0-1 means the unwrap was replaced.
Fix: never run Pack Islands / Re-Unwrap / Smart UV Project on tiling landscape pieces or grass. If it already happened, re-import the original NIF (or a backup) and redo the edits, or copy the old UVs back: when the triangles did not change, every triangle can be matched to the original by its corner positions and its UVs restored exactly. Do the restore in Blender too (re-import the fixed NIF), otherwise the next export from the same scene brings the broken UVs back.
Most common cause, found later the same day: one mesh in the export had no UV map. The exporter made a placeholder UV map with Edit Mode + Smart UV Project while the rest of the model was selected, and Blender's multi-object Edit Mode re-unwrapped every selected mesh. The exported NIF got squeezed UVs on most shapes (8 of 12 in a test) while the Blender scene still looked right, so the problem only showed in game. Fixed in the Mossy add-on 5.5.2: only the mesh without UVs is unwrapped. Same trap by hand: never run Smart UV Project or Unwrap with several objects in Edit Mode unless all of them should be unwrapped.
Also seen: a solid cliff body on an alpha-blended decal material (an '8Bit' BGSM) only looked solid while its texture had no alpha; once the texture's vanilla alpha was back it turned see-through. Solid parts need an opaque material (blending, alpha test and decal off); only the fading decal pieces use the blended one.
A mesh that shows black in Blender has usually lost its UV map. The Mossy add-on (5.5.2) now gives such a mesh its original UVs back on export, matched triangle by triangle from the game's copy of the NIF or the NIF it was imported from, and says so in the export message; only when the mesh was changed too much does it fall back to a placeholder unwrap, with a warning that the texture will not line up.

verified_by: 2026-11-11: a cliff NIF re-exported from Blender: cliff UVs went from -4.11..5.08 to 0.6..0.99 and grass cards from -0.17..1.22 to 0..0.91; all 365/59/424 cliff triangles and 320 triangles on each of five grass cards matched the originals by corner position with zero UV conflicts, and copying the old UVs back restored them exactly.

title: Hard straight edges where a cliff or mound meets the ground: the decal pieces' fade is ignored because their material does not blend
content:
Hard straight edges where a cliff or mound meets the ground: the decal pieces' fade is ignored because their material does not blend
Symptom: at the foot of a dirt cliff or mud mound you see dark slabs with straight, sharp edges lying on the ground instead of patches that fade into the terrain. Retexturing the ground (even with seam fixes) does not help.
How vanilla blends these models: besides the mound itself, the NIF has flat decal pieces lying on the ground (for example GSDirtCliffLarge01 has Object007:1 with GlowingSeaCorrosion01_Alpha.BGSM and Object007:15 with GlowingSeaRubble01Decal8Bit.BGSM). Their edges fade out through vertex alpha (128 of 220 and 37 of 51 vertices below full alpha), the NIF has a blending NiAlphaProperty (flags 0x10ED and 0x12ED, threshold 128), the Decal shader flag is set, and the BGSM has alpha blending on (mode Standard, blend 6/7), Decal and Decal No Fade on; the Rubble one also uses alpha test 128.
Cause: a retexture mod pointed those decal pieces at an opaque material (a cliff or ground BGSM with alpha blending and alpha test off). The game uses the BGSM's alpha settings, so the vertex-alpha fade in the mesh is ignored and every patch is drawn solid.
Fix: keep the texture but give the decal pieces their own copy of the material with the vanilla decal settings: alpha blend on (Standard, 6/7), Decal and Decal No Fade on, alpha test on with 128 only for the 8-bit rubble style piece. Point only the decal shapes at the copy (for example GSMuckCliff02_Decal.bgsm), never change the shared material in place, because the cliff body uses it opaque. Set the Decal shader flag on those shapes in the NIF too.
How to find them: look for shapes that have vertex colors with alpha near 0 and a NiAlphaProperty with blending, but whose BGSM has blending and alpha test both off.
tags: seams hard edges ground decal fade cliff mound ground patch straight edges alpha blend decal flag vertex alpha bgsm retexture glowing sea corrosion rubble decal8bit
verified_by: 2026-11-11: vanilla GSDirtCliffLarge01.nif and its BGSMs read from the unpacked game (vertex alpha, NiAlphaProperty flags, BGSM blend/decal settings); a retextured copy had both decal pieces on an opaque cliff or ground BGSM; a scan of 19 NIFs found 4 such shapes in 2 NIFs.

title: Glowing plant does not show in game after a Blender export; it comes back when the NIF Emissive Color is set to black
content:
Glowing plant does not show in game after a Blender export; it comes back when the NIF Emissive Color is set to black
Symptom: a glowing plant or mushroom that uses a BGSM (Glow Map and Own Emit on) stops showing in game after it was exported from Blender. In NifSkope its BSLightingShaderProperty has a coloured Emissive Color (the BGSM's glow colour, for example #a953ff); setting Emissive Color back to 0,0,0 makes it show again.
Cause: when PyNifly imports a NIF it reads the BGSM and fills the Blender material's emission tint from the BGSM's Emittance colour. Exporters that copy that tint back into the NIF write the BGSM colour into the NIF's Emissive Color, while the original file had black. Tested in game: the coloured version did not show, the black version did.
Rule: when a shape uses a BGSM, the glow belongs in the BGSM (Emit Enabled, Emittance colour, Glow Map) and the NIF's Emissive Color can stay black. That is a normal vanilla layout: 596 vanilla glow-map shapes with a BGSM have black there. Shapes with no material file keep their NIF colour, because there the NIF is the material.
Fix: the Mossy Blender add-on (5.5.2) now writes black Emissive Color on every shape that uses a BGSM or BGEM, on every export, so it no longer has to be fixed by hand in NifSkope. For files already exported, set Emissive Color to 0,0,0 in NifSkope on those shapes; leave the BGSM's glow settings as they are.
tags: emissive color glow plant invisible not showing in game after export blender nifskope black bgsm emittance own emit glow map mushroom fungus
verified_by: 2026-11-11: in-game A/B by a modder on glowing fungus plants (coloured NIF Emissive Color: not shown; 0,0,0: shown); vanilla catalog of BSLightingShaderProperty shapes with Glow Map + Own Emit + BGSM: 596 black, 1,100 coloured; original mod NIFs had black; add-on export verified to write 0,0,0.

title: Plant disappears in Blender (only the selection outline is left) right after clicking Wind
content:
Plant disappears in Blender (only the selection outline is left) right after clicking Wind
Symptom: a plant imported from a NIF looks fine in Blender until Wind is applied; then its textured surface vanishes from the viewport and only the orange selection outline is left. Nothing is wrong with the mesh or the textures.
Cause: Wind stores the sway amount in the mesh's vertex alpha (the VERTEX_ALPHA colour attribute PyNifly exports as vertex alpha): 0 at the base, rising toward the tips. With the BGSM's Tree flag on, Fallout 4 reads vertex alpha as sway. But the Blender material PyNifly built on import still feeds VERTEX_ALPHA into its AlphaProperty node as transparency with an alpha cutoff of about 0.5, so every part that sways less than half is cut away in the viewport. PyNifly itself leaves that link out when it imports a tree material, for the same reason.
Fix: the Mossy Blender add-on (5.5.2) takes the Vertex Alpha link out of the material preview when Wind is applied and puts it back when wind is removed. Only the viewport changes: the exported NIF is byte-identical with or without the link. By hand: in the Shader Editor, remove the link from the 'Vertex Alpha' attribute node into the AlphaProperty node's 'Vertex Alpha' input.
Related: in game the same sway values show up as transparency (half the plant invisible) when the material's Tree flag is off, so wind plants need a BGSM with Tree on.
tags: wind plant disappears invisible blender viewport only outline vertex alpha transparency alphaproperty pynifly tree flag sway leaf card
verified_by: 2026-11-11: a modder's saved Blender scene (fungus plant after Wind): EEVEE render 0 visible pixels with the Vertex Alpha link, 1,535 without; NIF exported both ways byte-identical; PyNifly nif/shader_io.py skips the link for FO4 tree materials.

title: Part of the model is missing after exporting a plant from Blender (custom mesh added next to the original game mesh)
content:
Part of the model is missing after exporting a plant from Blender (custom mesh added next to the original game mesh)
Symptom: you import a plant NIF, add your own mesh (for example extra leaf cards) next to the original game mesh, give your mesh wind and export. In game or NifSkope only your mesh is there; the original stock is gone.
Cause: exporting the selected object writes a NIF with just that object. The other shapes the imported NIF had (here the original stock, a BSMeshLODTriShape with its LOD levels) are left out, and saving over the original file loses them.
Fix: the Mossy Blender add-on (5.5.2) exports the whole model when the selected mesh sits under an imported NIF root next to other visible meshes, and says which pieces it included; hidden pieces stay out and are named. With an older add-on, select every piece of the model (or use the export that combines the selected meshes) before exporting.
Wind on only one piece: only the meshes that sway should get the Tree_Anim shader flag and a Tree material; vanilla wind NIFs (BSLeafAnimNode root) leave non-swaying parts without Tree_Anim (397 such shaders). The add-on now sets Tree_Anim only on the wind meshes' materials, so the original stock keeps its own material and does not sway.
Note: External Emittance in a BGSM is copied into the NIF's Shader Flags 1 (bit 29) by the exporter. No vanilla landscape material (0 of 485) uses it; if it is on in a plant's BGSM, that is the material's own setting.
Texture paths in the NIF: vanilla NIF texture sets write 'Textures\Landscape\Plants\X_d.dds' (raw scan of 1,709 vanilla landscape NIFs: 7,284 paths with the Textures\ prefix, none with forward slashes). BGSMs write 'Landscape/Plants/X_d.dds'. If one slot of a NIF texture set (often the glow map) shows the BGSM form, change it to the NIF form; the add-on (5.5.2) now does this on export.
tags: export missing piece part of model gone custom mesh original mesh plant stock leaf card blender nif bsmeshlodtrishape wind tree_anim external emittance texture path glow map textures prefix forward slash nifskope texture set
verified_by: 2026-11-11: a plant NIF with a custom wind mesh plus the original BSMeshLODTriShape stock: the single-object export kept 1 of 2 shapes; with the fix the same scene exports both, root BSLeafAnimNode, Tree_Anim only on the wind shape; vanilla catalog: 1,359 Tree_Anim shapes, 0 with External Emittance; 0 of 485 vanilla landscape BGSMs use External Emittance.

title: Blender error "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'collision_type'" (or 'slot', 'preset') in the Mossy add-on's panels
content:
Blender error "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'collision_type'" (or 'slot', 'preset') in the Mossy add-on's panels
Older versions of the Mossy Blender add-on (before 5.4.5) could print errors like AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'collision_type' from ui_panels.py in Blender's console, and a panel (for example LOD & Collision) failed to draw.
Cause: many of the add-on's tools register about 3 seconds after Blender starts (or on the first change to the scene). Until then Blender hands the panel nothing for those buttons, and the panel crashed setting an option on them. It is harmless: the error stops once those tools have loaded. If it keeps repeating long after start-up, the delayed tools failed to load; check Blender's system console (Window > Toggle System Console) for messages after 'Phase 2'.
Version 5.4.5 fixes it: the buttons always draw and get their options once the tools exist.

verified_by: Reproduced 2026-11-03 by drawing every panel in background Blender before the delayed tools registered: 7 panels failed before the fix, 0 after.

title: Mossy Blender add-on: tools add to a mesh's textures and materials, never replace them (5.4.5)
content:
Mossy Blender add-on: tools add to a mesh's textures and materials, never replace them (5.4.5)
Since version 5.4.5 every tool in the Mossy Blender add-on that touches a material only adds to what the mesh already has: material setup, Install Texture, Auto-Connect Textures, applying a .bgsm, Material Browser presets, Setup HD Material, Set Up as Leaf Card, joining meshes / Combine Vegetation, Apply Displacement and image import. Existing texture files are never written over when textures are copied or converted.
Older versions could, mostly on meshes loaded from a NIF: swap the material for an empty one, plug a new shader into the material output (the original textures were still in the node tree but no longer connected), delete the other materials after a join, turn leaves one-sided when a .bgsm was applied, or write over an existing .dds. If textures vanished after using one of those tools in an older version, open the Shader Editor: the original image nodes (Diffuse_Texture etc.) are often still there and can be reconnected, or reload the NIF.
Also fixed in 5.4.5: exporting had not created any new .bgsm files since 5.4.0 (existing ones were kept, new materials never got one).
Tools whose job is to put a new texture in a slot still do so when asked: Install Texture with a file you pick, Generate + Apply Texture, Wrap Image, baking AO into the diffuse, and picking a glow map. 'Mark as Collision Mesh' still clears that mesh's materials, as collision needs none.

title: A tree whose leaves are part of the trunk mesh (AI-made or baked tree): collision and wind in Fallout 4
content:
A tree whose leaves are part of the trunk mesh (AI-made or baked tree): collision and wind in Fallout 4
Many AI-generated or baked trees are ONE mesh with ONE material: the trunk, branches and leaves are joined. Tools that split by loose parts or by material then see a single piece, which causes two problems:
- Collision: one convex hull around the whole tree, so the player bumps into an invisible wall around the leaves. Vanilla trees do not do that. Measured on the unpacked game: BlastedForestFungalTreeLarge01 has about 9 separate convex pieces along the trunk, root flare and crown masses, smaller than the visible tree (794 x 747 units against 1118 x 1238); BlastedForestBurntTreeUpright01 has one tight piece around the trunk (154 x 195 against 288 x 366). Leaves get no collision.
- Wind: painting the wind by height (or along the whole piece) makes the trunk sway as much as the leaves. Vanilla trees with wind that are one shape (TreeElmForest01, TreeElmFree01, TreeMapleInstitute01Green) keep the bottom 20% at 0 and paint by distance from the trunk: 0.03-0.06 next to the trunk even high up, about 0.2-0.4 a little way out, up to 0.9-1.0 at the outer canopy. Trees made of separate shapes (TreeMapleForest1) put the trunk in a material without the Tree (wind) flag, so it never moves. The Glowing Sea trees TreeGS01/02 and the blasted trees have no wind at all.
You do not have to separate the leaves from the trunk. The Mossy Fallout 4 Blender add-on (5.5.2 and later) finds the solid woody parts itself: a face belongs to the trunk when a ray shot inward travels at least 3% of the tree's height before leaving the same solid (leaves are thin shells or flat cards).
- Add Collision, or Add Custom Collision on a tree that is too detailed for an exact mesh, then builds several compact convex hulls around the trunk, thick branches and root flare; the leaves get none. On a test tree: 5 hulls, about 27 times less volume than one hull over everything, 1% of leaf faces inside a hull. It exports as separate convex pieces with one physics system each.
- Wind with type Tree paints a one-piece tree by distance from the trunk surface at each height times height above the base, then evens out any edge where the weight would jump, so nothing stretches. On the test tree the trunk went from 0.28-0.91 to 0.00-0.06 while the leaves still move (up to about 0.9). Re-painted vanilla one-piece trees came out closer to Bethesda's own values than the older painting (38.7 against 43.5 of 255 average difference).
After changing a tree: redo the collision and the wind (Wind button), then export. A separate trunk and leaf mesh still works too and keeps the older per-piece painting.
